parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Amino acids can act as monomers.

State what is meant by the isoelectric point of an amino acid.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Electrophoresis can be used to separate and identify amino acids.

Table 4.3 shows information about the three amino acids glycine, lysine and glutamic acid.

Table 4.3

| amino acid | structural formula of amino acid | isoelectric point |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| glycine (gly) | $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{COOH}$ | 6.0 |
| lysine (lys) | $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2)\text{COOH}$ | 9.7 |
| glutamic acid (glu) | $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH})\text{COOH}$ | 3.2 |

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
A mixture containing these three amino acids is analysed in a buffer solution of $\text{pH}6.0$.

Draw and label **three** spots on Fig. 4.1 to indicate the predicted position of each of these amino acids, gly, lys and glu, after electrophoresis.
